title: Does a breeze help a towel dry?
hook: Cool day, wet towel on the line. Is a breeze any help?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that moving air carries damp air away from the cloth so more water can leave each part of it, without changing how much cloth is exposed

misconception: A breeze only helps drying if the air is warm.
objective: The model keeps cloth area fixed and changes the assumed mass-transfer flux. Area and transfer conditions multiply; changing one does not secretly change the other.

claims.text: The model keeps the cloth area fixed and changes only how fast the moving air takes water away. Area and air movement multiply; changing one does not secretly change the other.
claims.source: OpenStax College Physics 2e §13.6, https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/13-6-humidity-evaporation-and-boiling (opened 2026-10-14). Evaporation is inhibited by humidity. The card's constant flux is an explicitly illustrative assumption, not a measured household drying rate. claims.text: Title: Does a breeze help a towel dry? Hook: Cool day, wet towel on the line. Is a breeze any help? Question: Same towel, same cool air. Does a breeze make it dry sooner? Options: No: only warm air helps / Yes: moving air carries the damp away / Only if the breeze spreads it out. Correct option: Yes: moving air carries the damp away.
claims.source: Prediction line from company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md (wave W2, cm-lifehacks), numbers filled from home-models.ts case 'flux' at the starting input 1; option order varied for TP-8. Reset to unverified 2026-10-15 by demo-builder (r11 fix plan wave W2: new prediction line, stage and reveal; engine 2). Re-verify against the rebuilt stage. | FC pass 52 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, W-1144/W2): DISPUTED. The keyed option states a size the world does not fix. Question: 'Same towel, same cool air. Does a breeze make it dry sooner?' Key: 'Yes, about 2× sooner'. The direction is supported (OpenStax §14.6: air flow replaces saturated air and evaporation continues). The '2×' is not a property of breezes: it is the card's own setting (flux 2 against 1, home-lessons.ts values [2,1]), the same at every slider value, and c2 says it is 'an illustrative setting, not a measured benefit from any fan'. The question does not say 'in this model', so the learner is marked right for a number nothing measures. Real gains depend on air speed and on how wet the cloth still is. Fix (demo-builder, with cm-lifehacks for the prediction line): scope the question to the model, e.g. 'In this model a breeze sets the air to 2, still air to 1. Same towel: does it dry sooner?', or make the key 'Yes, sooner' with the 2× shown only on the stage. Re-check after the change. | Reset to unverified 2026-10-16 by demo-builder (batch B4, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/content-patch-2026-10-16-r2.md section 1): title, hook, options, answer replaced (row "breeze-is-not-extra-surface"). Not checked by the builder. | Source added by demo-builder 2026-10-16 (B4): OpenStax College Physics 2e §14.6 (air flow replaces the saturated air by dry air and evaporation continues), the support for the keyed outcome. | FC pass 61 (fact-checker, SO-10-2 Life Hacks set A, 2026-10-16; shared review server 5b2fee7, R3a pass; walkthrough on :3591 read first, cut at the appendix; numbers re-run in node from the engine on main 2d6b4d5): VERIFIED. Title, hook, question, options and answer 1 match home-lessons.ts and the rendered page. Key supported by OpenStax College Physics 2e §14.6 Convection, opened as CNXML (raw.githubusercontent.com/openstax/osbooks-college-physics-bundle/main/modules/m42229/index.cnxml, sha256 8d5d1f356fe442d5…): 'without air flow, the air becomes saturated and evaporation stops. Air flow caused by convection replaces the saturated air by dry air and evaporation continues.' The keyed option states only the direction; the 2× stays on the stage and reveal as the card's setting (c2). Record: company/reviews/lifehacks-200/2026-10-16-fact-check-pass61.md.

recall.question: A towel has 1.5 m² open to still air. A fan doubles the model's air setting. What happens in the model?
options: Area becomes 3 m² and the drying speed doubles
Area stays 1.5 m² and the drying speed doubles
Area stays 1.5 m² and the drying speed is unchanged
recall.why: Drying speed = open area × air setting. The fan changes the air setting, not the area, so the speed doubles while the area stays 1.5 m². A face folded shut stays hidden however the air moves. The doubling is the card's setting, not a fan measurement.
